problems.theorem_title: The Tate coordinates satisfy the Weierstrass equation
problems.formal_statement:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Reference.TateCurvesTheta.TateParameter.tatePoint_equation
    {k : Type*} [NormedField k] [CompleteSpace k] [IsUltrametricDist k]
    (t : TateParameter k) (h12 : (12 : k) ≠ 0) :
    t.TatePointEquation := by
  sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a complete nonarchimedean normed field in which $12\ne 0$, and let $q\in K^\times$ with $\lvert q\rvert<1$. Write $E_q$ for the Tate curve and $X(u),Y(u)$ for the Tate coordinate series at a unit $u\in K^\times$.

If $q^n u\ne 1$ for every integer $n$, then

$$
(Y(u))^2+X(u)Y(u)=(X(u))^3+a_4(q)X(u)+a_6(q).
$$

This equation supplies the affine points used by the Tate parametrization.

problems.theorem_title: The Tate point map sends products to sums
problems.formal_statement:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Reference.TateCurvesTheta.TateParameter.tatePoint_mul
    {k : Type*} [NormedField k] [CompleteSpace k] [IsUltrametricDist k] [DecidableEq k]
    (t : TateParameter k) (hmem : t.TatePointEquation)
    (h12 : (12 : k) ≠ 0) (h2 : ‖(2 : k)‖ = 1) (u v : kˣ) :
    t.tatePoint hmem h12 (u * v) = t.tatePoint hmem h12 u + t.tatePoint hmem h12 v := by
  sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a complete nonarchimedean normed field with $12\ne 0$ and $\lvert 2\rvert=1$. For $q\in K^\times$ with $\lvert q\rvert<1$, assume the Tate coordinate series $X(u),Y(u)$ satisfy the equation of $E_q$ for every $u\notin q^{\mathbb Z}$. Let $P_q:K^\times\to E_q(K)$ send each such $u$ to $(X(u),Y(u))$ and each power of $q$ to the point at infinity.

For all $u,v\in K^\times$,

$$
P_q(uv)=P_q(u)+P_q(v).
$$

The group law lets the parametrization descend to the quotient by $q^{\mathbb Z}$.

problems.theorem_title: The Tate point map is surjective
problems.formal_statement:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Reference.TateCurvesTheta.TateParameter.tatePoint_surjective
    {k : Type*} [NormedField k] [CompleteSpace k] [IsUltrametricDist k]
    (t : TateParameter k) (hmem : t.TatePointEquation)
    (h12 : (12 : k) ≠ 0) (h2 : ‖(2 : k)‖ = 1) :
    Function.Surjective (t.tatePoint hmem h12) := by
  sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a complete nonarchimedean normed field with $12\ne 0$ and $\lvert 2\rvert=1$. For $q\in K^\times$ with $\lvert q\rvert<1$, assume the Tate coordinate series satisfy the equation of $E_q$ off $q^{\mathbb Z}$. Write $P_q:K^\times\to E_q(K)$ for the point map from these series, taking each power of $q$ to the point at infinity.

Every point of the Tate curve is an image of a unit,

$$
\forall P\in E_q(K),\qquad \exists u\in K^\times,\quad P_q(u)=P.
$$

Surjectivity supplies the last step in identifying the analytic quotient with the group of points.
